thread:
incident-bot: Paging @jamal @sara — high 5xx rate from dedicated-us-west-1 pool, spike detected at 3790001100. Please investigate.

jamal: acked. I'll take this. grabbing quick impact numbers.

sara: thanks — any idea if autoscale kicked in?

jamal: current snapshot — qps ~3.2k (normal 800), 5xxs at ~12% of requests, avg latency 450ms -> tails 2s. Autoscaler shows pool at cap (reserved nodes) and burst toggle was off. looks like sudden noisy tenants + long sequences.

ingrid: if burst is off we can enable emergency burst to buy time. recommend: enable burst for 10m and concurrently apply customer-level throttles for unknown API keys.

jamal: running emergency commands now:
```
# enable emergency burst for dedicated-us-west-1
rictl pools set-burst --pool dedicated-us-west-1 --enable --duration 10m --reason "oncall emergency"
```

deploy-bot: policy-change: pools.dedicated-us-west-1.burst enabled (actor: jamal) — change_id=chg_20260317_379000. :white_check_mark:

jamal: burst enabled. immediate improvement at edge — latency 220ms, 5xxs down to ~4%. still seeing hotspots from a few API keys. proposal: apply temporary per-key rate caps and reduce default burst quota for public tier. enterprise customers get priority bump if impacted.

micah: customer-success here — list of customers showing errors: acme-inc (enterprise), fluxlabs (mid-market), many anonymous keys. acme reports timeouts. they should be protected first.

sara: agree. plan: 1) apply strict soft rate-limits for anonymous and new keys (50rps), 2) reduce default burst tokens for public tier to 25% of normal, 3) raise SLA enterprise token allotment for acme-inc. I'll own routing policy patch.

jamal: applying rate-limit change now:
```
# patch routing rules
rictl routing update --pool dedicated-us-west-1 --rule "if api_key.type==\"anonymous\" then set_rate_limit=50" --dry-run=false
rictl quotas set --scope public-tier --burst-tokens 0.25
rictl quotas bump --customer acme-inc --burst-tokens 2x --note "oncall mitigation"
```

deploy-bot: routing.update ok (actor: sara) — rule_id=r_379000_anoncap. quotas updated (actor: jamal). :white_check_mark:

jamal: after rate-capping anonymous keys errors dropped further to ~1.2%, overall latency stable. however we still see occasional head-of-line stalls caused by long sequences + reranking models. suggest disabling non-critical features (reranking & aggressive sampling) for public tier until traffic normalizes.

ingrid: +1 to disabling reranking for public. enterprise users unchanged. execute feature-flag flip.

jamal: flipping feature flags:
```
# disable reranking for public tier
rictl feature toggle --name reranking --scope public-tier --state off --reason "incident mitigation"
```

deploy-bot: feature.toggle applied (reranking -> OFF for public-tier) (actor: jamal) — toggle_id=tog_379000_rerank. :white_check_mark:

jamal: monitoring — 5xxs ~0.2%, p95 latency back to normal 120-150ms. burst still active for 8m left. will keep watching. planning handoff in 20m to @sara for sustained mitigation and comms.

sara: taking handoff. I'll keep burst enabled until load normalizes, then ramp down in controlled steps and re-enable reranking when we have headroom. I'll also coordinate customer comms with @micah.

micah: on it — prepping brief for acme-inc + FluxLabs. will propose temporary traffic allowances and explain mitigation steps.

jamal: leaving notes in incident doc and linking perf graphs. summary: cause = sudden traffic surge from noisy anonymous keys + long-sequence requests hitting reranking model; mitigations = emergency burst enabled, anonymous/key-level rate-limits, reduced public burst tokens, enterprise quota bump, reranking disabled for public.

sara: noted. follow-ups: postmortem + evals on autoscaler thresholds and safer default burst config; also add a playbook step to auto-apply anonymous key cap when pool OOMs.

customer-success: 👍 will be ready to send targeted emails once you confirm final status.

incident-bot: incident mitigated (mitigation_id=mit_379000). continue monitoring for 2 hours. if metrics regress, page oncall as usual.

jamal: handing off to @sara now. good job team :thumbsup:

sara: taking over. I'll post final resolution note and coordinate postmortem.

micah: thanks — will draft customer comms and flag high-priority accounts.
